name: Matra MS650 Longtail
description:
The Matra MS650 Longtail represents the French aerospace company's determined assault on international endurance racing in the late 1960s. Matra Sports, backed by the French government and drawing on its parent company's aviation expertise, developed this sleek Group 6 prototype to challenge the dominant Anglo-American machinery at Le Mans and beyond.

The MS650 was powered by Matra's own 3.0-liter V12 engine, a high-revving masterpiece that could scream to over 10,000 RPM. Producing 392 horsepower from just three liters, the all-alloy V12 was one of the most sophisticated racing engines of its era. The long-tail bodywork was specifically developed to maximize straight-line speed on high-speed circuits, reducing drag while maintaining stability at speeds exceeding 300 km/h.

Weighing just 740 kg, the MS650 featured a lightweight aluminum monocoque chassis that showcased Matra's aerospace engineering heritage. The combination of the screaming V12, aerodynamic efficiency, and featherweight construction made it a formidable competitor on fast circuits where its power-to-weight ratio and top speed could be fully exploited.

The MS650 was part of Matra's journey toward their historic Le Mans victories in 1972, 1973, and 1974. While those later triumphs came with different cars and Simca backing, the MS650 program laid the crucial groundwork, proving that a French manufacturer could compete at the highest level of international sports car racing.
